summary: Round 1 (new module, general p, unequal dimensions). Both MARKED statements are faithful: Déf. 2 (`IsCompatibleAssocPi σ f`: f·[m] = t·[(φᵢ m_{σ(i)})ᵢ], φᵢ : F(B_{σ(i)}) ≃ₜ F(Bᵢ) conical isomorphisms whose dimension equality is part of `IsConeIso`, t ∈ ℝ^{+p}/ℝ^+), the compatible automorphisms really form a subgroup (one/mul/inv, with the composition rule σ_{f∘g} = σ_g σ_f), and G_I has finite index ≤ p! UNCONDITIONALLY (cosets inject into Perm(Fin p)). Prop. 4: both assertions for nonempty (DEC-128) factors, hypotheses on the subgroup with Déf. 15's own predicates (IsPretransitive, IsBalayableFor), the first by the printed composite along the cycle of i₀, the second by finitely many fixed isomorphisms. ONE MAJOR: the SCOPE, two docstrings and REPORT question 1 assert that σ is NOT determined by f when equal-dimensional factors are single points, and state perm_unique, compatiblePerm and ker_compatiblePerm under [∀ i, Nontrivial (B i)]. That claim is false: f conjugates [c] to [c∘σ] (smul_torus) and the torus acts freely, so σ is unique for merely NONEMPTY factors — proved in /tmp/bzaud45xy/perm.lean in ~30 lines from the module's own lemmas. No Lean statement is false; the hypothesis is superfluous (and excludes the connected 0-dimensional « variété », a point), and the author is asked to accept a false premise as a « reading ». One minor: Déf. 2's « si l'on définit un automorphisme φ de la structure conique affine du produit par la formule » (that the permuted formula IS a conical automorphism) is neither proved nor disclosed here. kb/0002 clean; no instance declared.

checks.perm_uniqueness: perm_unique, compatiblePerm, ker_compatiblePerm carry [∀ i, Nontrivial (B i)], justified by « with one-point factors of equal dimension [σ] is not [unique]: every permutation of equal-dimensional one-point factors represents the same automorphisms ». FALSE. If f is associated with σ and σ', smul_torus gives piTorusAut [c∘σ] • p = f • [c] • f⁻¹ • p = piTorusAut [c∘σ'] • p; the torus acts freely (eq_one_of_piTorusAut_smul_eq), so (c∘σ')⁻¹(c∘σ) is diagonal for every c; with c = 2 at σ i and 1 elsewhere, σ i ≠ σ' i makes that ratio 2 at i and 1/2 at σ'⁻¹(σ i) ≠ i — not diagonal. Concretely, for p = 2 and two points of dimension 0, PiBase ≅ ℝ₊* (the ratio), id-associated automorphisms are r ↦ tr and swap-associated ones r ↦ t/r: disjoint. /tmp/bzaud45xy/perm.lean proves `perm_unique_of_nonempty [∀ i, Nonempty (B i)] … : σ = σ'` (axioms the standard three). Note that for a CONNECTED « variété » of dimension 0 (a point) the current hypothesis excludes the factor entirely

issues.problem: A false mathematical claim is recorded and put to the author as a « reading, not finding »: that the permutation of a compatible automorphism is not determined when equal-dimensional factors are single points. It is always determined for nonempty factors (torus equivariance + freeness; proof in /tmp/bzaud45xy/perm.lean). As a consequence the homomorphism G → Perm(Fin p) and ker = G_I are stated under a superfluous hypothesis that excludes connected 0-dimensional factors. The Lean statements themselves are true
